items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: I'm trying to think of that guy that danced. He had his wife and she was a singer and that's the first show I arranged for him at the Lafayette Theatre, that's in '28 and then I arranged for Ethel Waters.

ctx.x: How did you meet Lucky Roberts and all that.

I used to go up to Lucky's place, see, and listen to Lucky and everything and Lucky knew me so he asked me if I wanted a job and that's when I got it. But when Small's opened up, no, this is before Small. See, I had a band over there in Brooklyn and the guy owed me a week's salary and we opened up that Monday night and he said he was going to pay me and he didn't pay me, so I said well, it's no music. He said, no -- I said to the fellows, don't you play. He pay me, we play. If he don't don't. So I take all my…
You weren't talking about Butterbeans and Susie.
